genZNote: Broad-based budding is the tell. Narrow-based budding means you're looking at something else entirely.

morphology.shape: Dimorphic: mold form at room temperature, thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding at body temperature
morphology.notes: The broad-based bud (a wide connection between mother and daughter cell) is a distinctive diagnostic feature

habitat.naturalHabitat: Moist soil rich in organic/decaying matter, often near waterways
habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental saprophyte; opportunistic and sometimes primary pathogen even in immunocompetent hosts
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Endemic to the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys and the Great Lakes region of North America
habitat.reservoir: Soil, decaying wood/vegetation in endemic regions

microscopy.stain: KOH prep or Giemsa/methenamine silver stain of tissue/sputum
microscopy.appearance: Thick-walled yeast with characteristic broad-based budding in tissue

culture.media: Sabouraud dextrose agar (mold form, 25-30°C); enriched blood agar (yeast form, 37°C)
culture.growthCharacteristics: Slow growing — mold form can take 1-4 weeks
culture.colonyMorphology: White to tan, cottony mold colonies at room temperature; wrinkled, waxy yeast colonies at 37°C

identificationClues: Broad-based budding yeast on direct microscopy of tissue/sputum — the classic diagnostic clue
Thermal dimorphism (mold at room temperature, yeast at 37°C)
Urine/serum antigen testing available and faster than culture
Exposure history in the Ohio/Mississippi River valley or Great Lakes region

diseases: Pulmonary blastomycosis (can mimic bacterial pneumonia or malignancy)
Cutaneous blastomycosis (verrucous or ulcerative skin lesions)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Inhalation of conidia from disturbed moist soil, often near rivers/waterways
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic to the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys and the Great Lakes region of North America; unlike many systemic fungal infections, causes significant disease even in immunocompetent hosts
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Direct visualization of broad-based budding yeast in tissue is often diagnostic and faster than waiting for the slow-growing culture

examFacts.importantTest: Direct microscopy showing broad-based budding yeast; urine/serum antigen test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Broad-based budding, distinguishing it microscopically from the narrow-based budding of Cryptococcus and other yeasts
